title: Stock Market Today Highlights, August 5: Sensex rises 152 points, Nifty ends above 24,620 after RBI keeps repo rate unchanged - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Highlights - Find here all the updates related to Sensex, Nifty, BSE, NSE, share prices and Indian stock markets for 5th August 2026.

Indian equity benchmarks ended marginally higher on Wednesday as investors welcomed the Reserve Bank of India’s decision to keep the repo rate unchanged at 5.25 per cent while raising its FY27 GDP growth forecast and lowering the inflation outlook.

The Sensex gained 152.05 points to close at 78,581, while the Nifty 50 ended 9.75 points higher at 24,624.65. Markets trimmed early gains as crude oil prices rose amid renewed geopolitical tensions in West Asia.

Realty and auto stocks outperformed on expectations of festive-season demand and supportive financing conditions, while metal shares advanced on optimism over stronger domestic growth.

Analysts said the RBI’s balanced policy stance reinforced confidence in India’s macroeconomic resilience despite global uncertainties.

The rupee strengthened 13 paise against the US dollar, adding to positive sentiment.

Market experts expect the Nifty to remain range-bound near the 24,650 resistance level, with stock-specific opportunities likely to drive near-term gains.

* Sensex: up 152.05 points (+0.19%) to 78,581.00

* Nifty 50: up 9.75 points (+0.04%) to 24,624.65

* RBI policy: Repo rate unchanged at 5.25%; neutral policy stance retained

* Macro outlook: RBI raised FY27 GDP growth forecast and lowered inflation projection

* Sector winners: Realty, auto and metal stocks led gains

* Market driver: Early optimism on RBI policy offset by higher crude oil prices amid West Asia tensions

* Crude oil: Brent above $80.69 a barrel during trade

* Rupee: Appreciated 13 paise to 95.15 per US dollar (provisional)

* Technical view: Nifty faces immediate resistance near 24,650; analysts expect stock-specific action in the near term

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has marginally bumped up real GDP growth projection for FY27 to 6.7 per cent from earlier estimate of 6.6 per cent. It slightly revised lower the CPI inflation for FY27 to 5.0 per cent from earlier estimate of 5.1 per cent.

RBI raises FY27 GDP growth forecast to 6.7% and lowers CPI inflation projection to 5%, amid resilient economic indicators.

Godrej Agrovet reported standalone PAT of Rs 183.60 crore in Q1FY27 as against Rs 168.89 crore in Q1FY26.

On consolidated basis, it dipped to Rs 128.31 crore.

Board approved the appointment of Ravishankar A. as the “Chief Financial Officer – Designate” with effect from September 21, 2026 upto September 30, 2026 and as the “Chief Financial Officer” of the Company with effect from October 1, 2026.

Benchmarks settled marginally flat. Sensex settled 152.05 pts or 0.19% positive at 78,581; Nifty 50 inched up 9.75 pts or 0.04% to 24,624.65.

EAAA, the alternatives arm of Edelweiss, through its flagship commercial real estate fund - Rental Yield Plus (RYP) - today announced the acquisition of a Grade A office Park in Pune, spanning approximately 1.0 million sq. ft. of gross leasable area. The acquisition expands the portfolio of RYP to 5.2 million sq. ft., including around 1.0 million sq. ft. under binding contracts.

“Today’s RBI decision to hold rates at 5.25 per cent was on expected lines and markets are unlikely to see any sharp reaction. The GDP upgrade to 6.7 per cent for FY27 is a quiet confidence signal on the domestic growth outlook, reflecting the resilience of the Indian economy despite a challenging global environment. The MPC’s acknowledgement of robust domestic demand, sustained government capital expenditure, and a well-capitalised banking system further reinforce this constructive view. Inflation is a near-term watch item, but the trajectory remains one of moderation beyond Q3. Rate-sensitive sectors, banking, NBFCs, real estate, and capital goods, remain well positioned with fundamentals intact, supported by stable borrowing costs and favourable financing conditions. For the broader market, this policy reinforces a supportive macro backdrop. We remain constructive, with financials, industrials, metals and consumption-oriented sectors offering the most compelling opportunities. Volatility, if any, should be used as an entry point rather than a reason for caution.”

“The RBI’s measures are a positive step towards ensuring that liquidity reaches the real economy without compromising financial discipline. A stable interest-rate environment, coupled with continued liquidity support, creates a conducive backdrop for credit expansion. For the residential real estate sector, easier availability of construction finance is as important as home loan affordability. As capital becomes more accessible, developers with strong balance sheets, sound governance and proven execution should be better positioned to accelerate project delivery, supporting both housing supply and broader economic growth. Affordable home loan will help in sustaining the residential demand and support project level liquidity for developers. We believe these measures will improve credit confidence across the ecosystem and sustain momentum in India’s housing market.”

An unchanged repo rate provides a stable market condition for the real estate sector, where investment decisions are inherently long term. Buyers, today are evaluating projects on the basis of infrastructure, connectivity and overall value, and policy stability complements that decision-making process. For developers, it brings greater visibility in financial planning and project execution. With demand remaining steady across emerging growth corridors, the current policy stance is likely to reinforce confidence and support sustained activity in the residential market. -
